text: This isn't a technical demo for other DBAs. It's a presentation back to Overlook's board — the same board that read about a competitor's breach and asked, could that happen to us? They want a direct answer in business terms, backed by the real proof this chapter already produced.

The structure maps straight back to the original mandate: restate the board's four deliverables, show the DR proof with real numbers from an unannounced drill, show the security and compliance proof, show the automation proof, and name one honest trade-off plainly — the secondary database's real ongoing cost.

The board doesn't need a list of Azure resources. They need the translation: Overlook can now lose at most 44 seconds of data and be back up in under 20 minutes during an actual outage, proven in a test nobody scheduled or rehearsed. That's a sentence a board can act on.

A presentation with zero caveats reads as either incomplete or dishonest to a board sophisticated enough to have asked these questions in the first place. Next lesson wraps up everything this capstone built, and where to go from here.
